page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a right margin note beside its last lines. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword at the lower right, below the last line. Faint bled-through text in the left and right margins is show-through and is not transcribed.

p.i: siterunt: Sed sunt & hæ mortuæ, nihilque docere possunt quum deest Spiritus Christi, qui unus in omnem veritatem inducit. Quare quod hic Psaltes de divina lege encomium cecinit, de ea, ut a mentibus Spiritu superno donatis percipitur, intelligendum est, non ut scripto tantum comprehenditur. Hic autem ubi Spiritus adest, effari non potest, quantum frugis optimæ adferat diligens & sedula Scripturarum & lectio & excussio: ut non injuria Paulus suum Timotheum tantopere incumbere illi voluerit, tantumque fructuum promiserit.

main_text.p: At vero NB nullis id rationibus ita ut experimento percipi potest: quan-quam pio homini, vel præsens Psaltis encomium, aut Pauli elogium quod adduximus, vel Moscheh testimonium Deut. iv. 6. satis probent nullum esse scripti genus quod vel dignitate, vel fructu ulla ex parte divinæ Scripturæ, quam jure vocamus, conferri queat.

Sed, ut dixi, NB experientia hic omni ratione potior est: ea pios animos ita Scripturæ arcanæ de Deo nostro ubique præclare testanti, & de ejus nos voluntate erudienti addicit, sic reddit affectos, ut plane comparatos se sentiant uti de se Vates in sequentibus canit. Desiderabilia præ auro &c. verf. 11 & 12. Sentiunt siquidem hi quam adversetur huic felicitati omnis naturæ nostræ sensus & conatus. Nihil siquidem est quod Dei apertius & potentius admoneat, judiciorum & operum ejus rationem plenius explicet, quam Sacræ Scripturæ: non tamen quibusvis, sed timentibus Deum, & Spiritu cælesti præditis. Expertus sum &c. Finge tibi aliquos, qui ratione naturali utuntur tanquam principio, ad maximam, quæ per naturam acquiri potest, venisse verborum rerumque cognitionem, & quid in Scripturæ intellectione præstituri sint, quoniam Theologi, te scilicet autocrato-Velthuisen de Usu Rar. in Theol. 132. rice id dictante, admodum falluntur & nimium sibi assumunt, cum hujusmodi controversias, quomodo sc. in Adamo omnes peccasse, concupiscentia peccatum dici queat, determinare volunt quamvis si ullum, hoc

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment ("siterunt:") that continues from the previous page; kept as a fragment. The "¶" mark before "At vero" is read as a paragraph break. "venisse" is read as printed "venille"; the printed form is uncertain at this point. "Disciept." in the running head is printed as shown and may be a printing error for "Disput."/"Discept.". Faint bled-through text in both margins (show-through from the facing page) is not transcribed. The right-margin note "Velthuisen de Usu Rar. in Theol. 132." is a printed note.
